title: Pick the right product, the right market, and your paperwork base
course_title: Export Readiness (Selected Products): From Local Seller to First Export Shipment

say: Pick the right product, the right market, and your paperwork base.
This is the video for Module 1 of Export Readiness.
Exporting means a buyer in another country receives your goods legally, in good condition, at a price that still pays you. A product that sells well in Ibadan may be a poor export.

panel.heading: Choose the product before the country

say: So choose one product first. Then pick one market with a simple scorecard. Then check the registrations and permits you need before any foreign buyer can receive your goods.

panel.heading: Choose the product before the country

say: Freight is charged mostly by weight. A product worth a lot per kilogram, like an adire scarf, carries freight easily.

panel.heading: Can this product travel?
items: Rules: food and cosmetics are strictest

say: Shipping can take weeks, so the product must stay good. Keep dated samples in final packaging and check them every month. A written record, not a guess.

panel.heading: Can this product travel?

say: Glass jars break. And food and cosmetics face the strictest rules abroad.

say: Last, supply. Offer a buyer the volume of your worst recent month, not your best. Failing on the second order damages trust more than a smaller honest answer.

say: Every product crossing a border has an HS code, a customs number. Duties and paperwork depend on it, so confirm it with your forwarder. Whole and ground ginger can sit on different lines.

say: Free tools from the International Trade Centre help. Trade Map shows which countries import your product. Market Access Map shows duties and requirements.

say: Then build a weighted scorecard. Choose criteria such as demand, ease of rules, logistics cost and buyer contacts. Score each country and multiply by the weight.

say: Check that your weights add up to 100%. And score rules so that easier means higher, so every high number is good.

panel.rule: Weights must add up to 100%. Easier rules get a higher score.

say: For example, Amina in Kaduna dries ginger. Her weights are demand 30%, rules 25%, logistics 20%, and contacts 25%. Ghana scores highest, 3.65.

Good demand, but hard rules and the most costly logistics.

say: Now your Nigerian base. Register your business with CAC. Register as an exporter with NEPC. Your bank processes Form NXP, so export payments come back through the banking system.
Then find your regulator. NAQS for plant products, NAFDAC for food and cosmetics, SON for standards. Ask your buyer in writing which documents their country needs.

panel.heading: Tick only what you actually hold
items: Bank ready to process Form NXP

say: Abroad, a missing certificate can hold goods at the port while charges grow. So check every document twice. And verify every buyer, for example on Companies House for UK firms, and speak by video call.

panel.heading: Real buyer or warning sign?
right: Asks you to pay a fee first
Wants goods on credit at once

say: Real buyers do not ask suppliers to pay for their import permits. Beware of payments bigger than the invoice with a request to send back the difference. Never ship on credit to a first-time buyer you cannot verify.

panel.heading: Real buyer or warning sign?

say: To remember. Choose the product first. Offer the volume of your worst month. Confirm your HS code, and let a weighted scorecard pick one market.
Build your CAC, NEPC and bank base, and never pay fees to a buyer.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Product first: value, shelf life, rules, supply

Never pay fees to a buyer
